beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three trays of cookies. How many cookies altogether?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One cookie, two cookies, three cookies...

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each tray holds five. Equal groups have the same number in each group.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count whole trays: five, ten, fifteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three fives make fifteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Another tray, another five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And another. And another.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: That's a lot of fives to write!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the trays: one, two, three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six groups, with five in every group.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: We have six fives. Write the five just once.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And write how many of them: six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six groups of five. We read this as six times five.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Same cookies. A shorter sentence!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more tray. Seven groups. Still five in each.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One more five! Thirty becomes thirty-five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try four trays with six cookies on each.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four and six... ten?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four plus six counts this picture: four cookies beside six cookies.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten cookies, on two unequal trays.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here are four trays of six. Count a six for every tray.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six, twelve, eighteen, twenty-four.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The four counts trays! It means four sixes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Groups needn't be trays. Three bicycles, two wheels each.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three groups of two. Six wheels!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three times five is fifteen cookies altogether.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The first number counts the groups.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The second counts how many are in each equal group.
